title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
keyIdea: In-order traversal (left, node, right) of a BST visits values in sorted order. Count down k at each visit; the node where k hits 0 is the answer. Stop early: once found, pass it straight up.

approaches.name: In-order into a list
approaches.idea: Collect every value in-order (sorted), return vals[k − 1].
approaches.why: Always visits every node and stores them all.

approaches.name: Iterative in-order with a stack
approaches.idea: Push while going left; pop = next smallest; k--; at 0 return; else go to its right child.
approaches.why: Stops after k pops; the stack holds at most one root-to-leaf path.

approaches.name: Recursive in-order, stop early
approaches.idea: left = recurse(left). -1 → this node is next: k--, if k == 0 return it; else recurse right. Not -1 → found below, return it.
approaches.why: Walks down to the smallest (h) then visits only k nodes before returning.

quiz.q: Why does in-order give the values in sorted order?
options: In a BST everything left is smaller and everything right is bigger, so left → node → right goes smallest to biggest
It only works for balanced trees

quiz.q: Why is k passed as int& in your code?
options: All calls must share one counter; by value each call would count on its own copy

quiz.q: Why is -1 safe as 'not found yet'?
options: Node values are 0…10⁴, so -1 can never be a real answer
Because the tree is a BST

quiz.q: What does 'return left;' do when left != -1?
options: The answer was found in the left subtree; pass it up without visiting this node or its right side

steps: Is k always valid (1…n)? Can values repeat? What range are the values?
